div.div: Why pod 3 would wait. The Deployment spreads its pods so that no node has more than one pod more than another, and a pod that can't keep to that stays Pending (DoNotSchedule). With one pod on worker1 and one on worker2, a third may only start on worker3, and worker3 has 489Mi of memory requests left against the 512Mi a pod asks for. Until someone frees about 25Mi there, or relaxes the rule to ScheduleAnyway, the HPA can ask for 3 pods and the site keeps running 2.

text.tspan: Why pod 3 would wait. The Deployment spreads its pods so that no node has more than one pod more than another, and a pod that can't keep to that stays Pending
(DoNotSchedule). With one pod on worker1 and one on worker2, a third may only start on worker3, and worker3 has 489Mi of memory requests left against the 512Mi a pod
asks for. Until someone frees about 25Mi there, or relaxes the rule to ScheduleAnyway, the HPA can ask for 3 pods and the site keeps running 2.
